title: Give and go from the wing
goal: A practitioner can read this play at a glance: Give and go from the wing.

rubric.must: The named scenario is visibly identified and its primary subject is clearly shown.
The picture visibly uses the required standard diagram structure and connected elements.
A reader can visually follow the principal flow or relationship from beginning to end.
Key labels remain legible and attached to the correct visible elements.
Lines and symbols do not visually imply unintended connections.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the playbook/basketball exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The drawing clearly presents “Give and go from the wing” on a standard half-court. Numbered players, ball, directional arrows, and four legible step labels show player 1 passing to player 2 on the wing, cutting toward the rim, receiving the return pass, and finishing with a layup.

items.evidence: The title names the play, the subtitle states the complete sequence, and the court visibly shows the give-and-go action.
A recognizable basketball half-court contains five numbered offensive players, a ball marker, basket, and distinct movement/pass/shot arrows explained by the legend.
The numbered labels and arrowheads make the sequence readable from 1: pass to wing, through 2: cut to rim and 3: return pass, to 4: layup.
The title, subtitle, player numbers, four action labels, and legend are visibly legible and positioned beside their corresponding actions.
Solid and dashed paths use visible arrowheads and distinct styles; their endpoints support the intended pass, cut, return pass, and layup without visibly implying an unintended player connection.
